text:
Alex: Orchid Systems POC update: customer wants Private deployment today. They asked for VPC peering (our control plane in Redwood acct) + single NAT for outbound. Need an exact handoff doc to send to their cloud eng.

Priya: Core items to request from the customer: 1) All customer CIDRs for apps and on-prem. 2) Prefer peering or PrivateLink? 3) Route table IDs to modify. 4) Subnet CIDRs where they'll place interface endpoints/peers. 5) NAT IPs for egress allowlist.

Alex: SOW contains 10.50.0.0/16 (apps) and 10.51.128.0/18 (onprem). They want peering.

Diego: Minimal routing details: on their side add route -> destination 10.200.0.0/16 (Redwood control plane CIDR) via peering-conn-id. On our side add route -> destination 10.50.0.0/16 via peering-conn-id. Confirm no overlapping prefixes.

Priya: Security caveats: do NOT accept propagated 0.0.0.0/0 into the peered RTB. If they use a NAT, ask for the NAT EIP(s) so we can permit model egress to external services.

Hannah: For management plane allowlist: TCP/443 from their peered subnets to our control-plane ENIs. We can either provide static ENI IPs (preferred) or request they open to the peered CIDR for the POC with a justification. Also include our cert fingerprint for any TLS-based attestations.

Diego: Pasteable AWS CLI examples for them: ```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0aa11bb22 --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc111
```and on our side:```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0cc33dd44 --destination-cidr-block 10.50.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc111
```Also run: ```bash
aws ec2 modify-vpc-peering-connection-options --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abc111 --requester-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true --accepter-peering-connection-options AllowDnsResolutionFromRemoteVpc=true
```Replace IDs.

Priya: Subnet planning: reserve two /24s for control-plane ENIs (multi-AZ spread) and one /24 for outbound NAT. Keep security groups minimal: HTTPS only from customer CIDRs; temporary SSH can be opened for debugging and then removed.

Hannah: If they prefer PrivateLink instead: they'll need to create interface endpoints in each AZ and accept our service name; DNS and SGs differ. PrivateLink avoids route table changes but takes more round-trips. For a fast POC peering tends to be quicker.

infra-bot: Checklist updated: awaiting peering acceptance by customer account. Automated deploys paused until connectivity is active.

Alex: Great. I'll send this with the AWS CLI snippets and ask for their RTB IDs and NAT EIPs. Will update thread when they accept. :thumbsup:
